meta.title: Energy-Based Transformers for Symbolic Music
meta.subtitle: Listening examples: continuation and attribute steering with an Energy-Based Transformer (EBT), compared with GPT-2 and Llama baselines.
meta.author: Rebecca Ceccatelli
meta.disclaimer: These are selected examples. In Unguided Generation and Single-Attribute Control, every clip was picked by ear by the author from the final evaluation outputs (the same pool as the listening study): they show what each system does at its best, not on average. The baselines there are Llama and GPT-2 trained with the same recipe as the EBT. Combined Control and Pushing Too Hard are not curated: every system gets the same prompt and its first sample, with the earlier Llama baselines. Leading silence is trimmed in the picked clips. The aggregate results are in the thesis.

sections.title: Unguided Generation
sections.intro: Each model gets the same short prompt (shaded) and continues it, with no control. All models are small and trained on GigaMIDI, once per tokenization; Llama and GPT-2 are trained with the same recipe as the EBT (same data, context length and number of training tokens). The REMI and Anticipation tabs are two tokenizations (see the ? next to Tokenization). The EBT generates each token by minimising a learned energy with a few gradient steps; Llama and GPT-2 are standard next-token predictors. Every continuation here was picked by ear.
sections.tabs_help: To learn music, a model reads it as a sequence of symbols (tokens), like a song spelled out with an alphabet. REMI and Anticipation are two such alphabets, called tokenizations. Every model is trained once with each.

sections.title: Single-Attribute Control
sections.intro: With a small regressor that predicts a musical attribute, generation can be steered toward a target without retraining. For the EBT, the regressor's error is added to the energy it already minimises, and λ sets how hard it pushes. The baselines steer Llama and GPT-2 (same training recipe as the EBT) with PPLM, Tilt or Best-of-N. Targets are given in standard deviations (SD) of the corpus, relative to each system's own unguided level. Every steered version here was picked by ear, at whatever strength and target sounded best, so several versions of one system can appear. In each card, the EBT's unguided sample is the one reference to listen against.
sections.tabs_help: To learn music, a model reads it as a sequence of symbols (tokens), like a song spelled out with an alphabet. REMI and Anticipation are two such alphabets, called tokenizations. Every model is trained once with each.

blocks.title: What do “SD” and “strength” mean?
blocks.text: SD (the target) = where you ask the music to go: “a bit louder” (+1 SD) or “much louder” (+2 SD); minus means the opposite direction. SD stands for standard deviation, how much loudness, note length or pitch usually varies between pieces.Strength (λ for the EBT; a strength or N for the baselines) = how hard the model is pushed to get there: how insistently you ask, not what you ask for.Think of throwing a ball at a target: the SD is where you aim, the strength is how hard you throw. Too soft and it falls short; too hard and it flies past and goes wild, which is what “Pushing Too Hard” shows.
blocks.teaser: How far each clip is pushed, and how hard

tabs.label: REMI
tabs.tabs_help: An attribute is the musical property being steered: velocity is how loud the notes are, duration is how long they are held (short and detached, or long and connected), and pitch register is how high or low they sit. Velocity can only be steered with REMI: Anticipation has no symbol for loudness.

sections.title: Combined Control
sections.intro: Two attributes steered at once, loudness and note length, in all four direction combinations (REMI tokenization only). The EBT simply adds one regressor energy per attribute; PPLM sums the two regressors' gradients, best-of-N the two distances, and tilting chains two tilts. Every tab uses the same prompt, so the unguided versions are identical and the tabs can be compared directly.

sections.title: Pushing Too Hard
sections.intro: Guidance strength is a trade-off. Past the recommended strength, strong EBT guidance flattens the model's choice among attribute values: the target is reached by scattering near-random notes. Harsh dissonance (share of simultaneous note pairs a semitone, major seventh or tritone apart) rises to the level of uniformly random notes, about 0.25.
sections.tabs_help: To learn music, a model reads it as a sequence of symbols (tokens), like a song spelled out with an alphabet. REMI and Anticipation are two such alphabets, called tokenizations. Every model is trained once with each.
